tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms and goals (endpoint failing, slow, scaling wrong, costs too much) rather than internal mechanics, and lists many explicit trigger contexts across real-time, serverless, async and batch transform scenarios. It also clarifies scope boundaries (what it does NOT cover). It is dense but stays within a reasonable paragraph length for the breadth of scenarios covered.
tests.evidence: Diagnose Amazon SageMaker inference that fails, errors, is slow, scales wrong or costs too much across real-time, serverless and asynchronous endpoints and batch transform jobs. Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific procedures (check-ids, API collection calls, metric namespaces) without explaining general concepts like what SageMaker or CloudWatch are. It assumes the agent already knows AWS basics and focuses on project-specific conventions (LLM-SM catalog, routing table, review procedure).
tests.evidence: "Grounded in [checks-sagemaker-inference.md]... load it when a symptom matches a row below. Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains a check-id index table and router table, but these are concise summary/index tables (one-line descriptions) pointing to references/ files for full detail, not large reference data blocks embedded in the body itself.
tests.evidence: "Load [checks-sagemaker-inference.md](references/checks-sagemaker-inference.md) before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six files in references/ (checks-sagemaker-inference.md, collection-reference.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md, api-quirks.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific condition or step for loading, e.g. loading api-quirks before interpreting clean/empty/InService responses, or known-causes when a user names a specific error.
tests.evidence: "Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, read-only constraints, severity rules) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while flexible areas like which area to focus on or how to phrase findings keep room for judgment while explaining the why behind the rules (e.g. two-namespace rule explanation).
tests.evidence: "You cannot conclude an endpoint is oversized, under-used, or idle from one namespace. The invocation metrics (AWS/SageMaker) tell you how much traffic and how fast; the instance resource metrics (/aws/sagemaker/Endpoints) tell you how hard the hardware is working."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task without a default; it consistently names specific AWS APIs to call for each check rather than offering alternative approaches.
tests.evidence: No menu-of-tools pattern found; e.g. "application-autoscaling:DescribeScalableTargets for the variant" is given as the single approach.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable approach (identify area, read config, check reliability, etc.) applicable to any endpoint or job, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. Each step depends on state gathered by the one before it, and each branches by area: run only the branches for the areas in scope."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section and an 'Error Handling' section with api-quirks traps, functioning as a gotchas section with concrete, specific corrections to assumptions the agent would otherwise make.
tests.evidence: "'The endpoint is InService, so it's serving traffic and the queue is fine.' InService is control-plane state; a real-time, async or serverless variant can be InService with CurrentInstanceCount = 0..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces health reports and provides three dedicated templates in assets/ for the different report types, referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: "[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full real-time endpoint report is requested."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; templates are stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally rather than embedded.
tests.evidence: Body only references templates via links in Step 8 and Appendix; no inline template skeleton is present.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three files in assets/ are linked in the SKILL.md body.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each asset link specifies the exact condition under which it should be loaded (full report requested for a specific area).
tests.evidence: "[serverless-async-health-report-template.md](assets/serverless-async-health-report-template.md) — load when a full serverless or async report is requested."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: All asset references use relative paths in the form assets/<filename>.md.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' format, and the detailed sections below use '### Step N — ...' headings that match the checklist step numbers.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources." ... "### Step 1 — Identify the area"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its own findings for correctness before presenting, covering check-id accuracy, observed-vs-inferred values, namespace coverage, and disclosure of gaps.
tests.evidence: "Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion." ... "Every cited value was actually observed, not inferred."
